title: The Integration Boost Invocation writes a Reward Code to the Integrator registry despite having no Reward Code among its own parameters
content:
A.2.2.9.2.2.3.6.4.1.2 specifies the Integration Boost's final registry output: update the List Of Current Integrators with the Integrator's name, its `Reward Code` "from the approved Proposal," and its `Tracking Methodology` "from the approved Proposal."

Neither field exists in this Primitive's own data. The Boost's Initial Planning Document (A.2.2.9.2.2.3.1.3) collects partner name, reward address, chain, cadence, data submission format, responsible actor, Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy and custom parameters — no Reward Code and no Tracking Methodology. The ratified Instance Configuration (A.2.2.9.2.2.3.6.3) copies exactly those same eight fields. The planning-stage registry write is consistent with this: A.2.2.9.2.2.3.1.4.1.1 adds only the Integrator Name to the Onboarding list, unlike the Distribution Reward's equivalent, which adds name *and* Reward Code (A.2.2.9.1.2.3.1.4.1.1).

The output clause therefore appears to be carried over from the Distribution Reward specification, where both fields are native. The substance is not incoherent — Reward Codes and Tracking Methodologies do apply to Integration Boost Partners, since A.2.2.9.2.2.1.4 has their balances also earn the Distribution Reward and A.2.2.9.2.2.1.4.1 makes the Boost's net-balance reporting a valid Tracking Methodology — but the Boost's own Invocation never captures either value, so the output names a source that does not exist within it.

Recording this is useful for the same reason as the directory divergence: it shows the two conforming Process Definitions were written in parallel with shared text rather than generated from a single model, which is the failure mode to watch as the schema is extended to the remaining Primitives.
description: Its Current Integrators output copies Reward Code and Tracking Methodology "from the approved Proposal", but neither field appears anywhere in the Boost's planning inputs or Instance Configuration.
